names.official: Impuesto sobre la renta y complementarios (personas naturales y jurídicas)
names.native: Impuesto sobre la renta y complementarios

taxes.base: Income of residents (worldwide) and of non-residents from Colombian sources: wages, business profits, capital income and occasional gains.
taxes.payer: Individuals and companies; withholding at source (retención en la fuente) collects most of it during the year.

rate.headline: Individuals 0%–39%; companies 35%
details: Individuals: seven UVT-based brackets at 0%, 19%, 28%, 33%, 35%, 37% and 39% (Estatuto Tributario art. 241, as amended by Ley 2277/2022). The 2026 UVT is COP 52,374.
Companies: general rate of 35%; financial entities pay additional points under Ley 2277/2022.
Retention (retención en la fuente) is an advance payment, not a separate tax; DIAN's collection statistics report it inside the income-tax total.

instruments.explanation: The largest national tax. Emergency decree 1474 of December 2025 tried to add a 15% surtax on financial-sector income and change wealth tax; the Constitutional Court struck the whole decree down in April 2026, so the pre-decree rules apply.
exceptions: Special regimes: SIMPLE (separate core), free-trade-zone and the 'régimen de zonas económicas'.

names.official: Impuesto sobre las ventas (IVA)

taxes.base: Sales of goods, provision of services and imports.
taxes.payer: Consumers; businesses collect it and take credits.

rate.headline: 19% general; 5% reduced; 0% on exports
details: Some basic goods are exempt or zero-rated; a 5% reduced rate applies to selected goods and services.
In January 2026 emergency decree 1474 briefly raised IVA on liquors to 19%; the Constitutional Court annulled it and the earlier rate applies again, with refunds ordered.

instruments.explanation: The second-largest national tax. DIAN reports it in three pieces: domestic returns, withholding on IVA and IVA on imports collected by customs; this core adds them together.
exceptions: Many basic foods, medicines and services are excluded or exempt; the lists are in the Estatuto Tributario.

names.official: Impuesto unificado bajo el Régimen Simple de Tributación (SIMPLE)

taxes.base: Gross income of small businesses and professionals opting into the regime (income up to 100,000 UVT).

rate.headline: Graduated rates by gross income and activity group
details: A single payment replaces income tax and, for enrolled taxpayers, the municipal ICA and the national consumption tax.

instruments.explanation: A simplified integrated tax that has grown quickly since 2019.
exceptions: Some professions and high earners cannot opt in.

names.official: Derechos de aduana (aranceles)

taxes.base: Customs value of imported goods, by tariff line.

rate.headline: 0% to about 40% by tariff line
details: Most industrial inputs face low tariffs; preferential rates apply under Colombia's trade agreements.

instruments.explanation: Duties collected by DIAN customs, reported separately from the IVA that is charged at the border.
exceptions: Trade agreements with the United States, the EU, the Pacific Alliance and others reduce or remove duties.

legalRefs.locator: art. 150-19-c (tariff regime set by Congress framework law)

names.official: Gravamen a los Movimientos Financieros (GMF)
names.native: Gravamen a los Movimientos Financieros – '4 por mil'

taxes.base: Withdrawals and transfers from bank and savings accounts and other financial transactions.

rate.headline: 0.4% (4 per thousand)
details: One account per person is exempt up to 350 UVT of monthly withdrawals.

instruments.explanation: A permanent tax on financial movements, an unusually productive tax in Colombia.
exceptions: Certain government and inter-bank transfers are exempt.

instruments.statusNote: Rules changed repeatedly in 2026: emergency decree 1474/2025 (annulled by the Constitutional Court in April 2026, C-079/26) and decree 173/2026 adopted under the second emergency (Decreto 150/2026), whose review by the Court is ongoing. Check the current text before relying on any threshold or rate.

names.official: Impuesto al patrimonio

taxes.base: Net worth above 72,000 UVT for individuals on 1 January (about COP 3.8 billion in 2026); 200,000 UVT for certain legal persons.

rate.headline: 0.5% – 1.5% of net worth for individuals (baseline Ley 2277/2022)
details: Baseline: 0.5% between 72,000 and 122,000 UVT, 1% from 122,000 to 239,000 UVT and 1.5% above.
A UVT is COP 52,374 in 2026.
2026 decrees changed the tax for legal persons; their current validity should be verified.

instruments.explanation: A permanent wealth tax created by the 2022 reform. It raises little revenue but is politically prominent.
exceptions: The main residence and shares of some companies are excluded up to limits.

names.official: Impuesto nacional al consumo

taxes.base: Restaurants and bars, mobile telephony and data services, and certain vehicles and other items.

rate.headline: 4%, 8% or 16% depending on the item
details: Restaurants 8%; mobile telephony and data 4%; vehicles 8% or 16% by price.

instruments.explanation: A single-stage tax, distinct from IVA, on a short list of consumption goods and services.
exceptions: Restaurants under the SIMPLE regime are exempt from the consumption tax.

names.official: Impuesto nacional a la gasolina y al ACPM
names.native: Impuesto nacional a la gasolina y al ACPM

taxes.base: Gallons of gasoline and ACPM (diesel) sold or imported.
taxes.payer: Producers and importers; passed on at the pump.

rate.headline: Fixed peso amount per gallon, adjusted for inflation
details: Set by law and indexed annually; the government has lowered effective yield when adjusting fuel prices.

instruments.explanation: A per-gallon national tax. Its collection fell in 2025 alongside a lower yield and price policy.
exceptions: Departments and municipalities also levy surcharges on gasoline.

names.official: Impuesto nacional al carbono

taxes.base: Carbon content of fossil fuels sold or imported, by tonne of CO₂ equivalent.

rate.headline: Peso amount per tonne of CO₂e, indexed annually
details: Companies can offset it by buying certified carbon credits.

instruments.explanation: An environmental tax on fossil-fuel emissions.
exceptions: Natural gas and LPG have exemptions.

names.official: Impuestos saludables: bebidas ultraprocesadas azucaradas y productos comestibles ultraprocesados

taxes.base: Sugary drinks by sugar content and ultra-processed foods high in sugar, sodium or saturated fat.
taxes.payer: Producers and importers; passed on in prices.

rate.headline: Ultra-processed foods 20% (from 2025); drinks per 100 ml by sugar content
details: The food tax rose from 10% in 2023 to 15% in 2024 and 20% from 2025.
Drinks pay a fixed peso amount per 100 ml, indexed to inflation.

instruments.explanation: Taxes introduced by the 2022 reform to discourage unhealthy consumption; their revenue was COP 3.3 trillion in 2025.
exceptions: Basic products and some categories are excluded; see the Estatuto Tributario for the current lists.

names.official: Cotizaciones al Sistema de Seguridad Social Integral (pensión, salud y riesgos laborales)

taxes.base: Monthly base salary (IBC) between one minimum wage and 25 minimum wages.

rate.headline: Pension 16% of IBC; health 12.5%; occupational risk by class
details: Pension: 12% employer + 4% employee; health: 8.5% employer + 4% employee, with employer health and parafiscal exemptions for wages under 10 minimum wages.

instruments.explanation: Compulsory contributions to pension funds, health insurers and risk insurers. They are administered by the pension and health systems, not the DIAN.
exceptions: The 2024 pension reform (Ley 2381 de 2024) has faced constitutional review; verify its current status before relying on any pension rule.

names.official: Aportes parafiscales (SENA, ICBF y cajas de compensación familiar)

taxes.base: Total payroll of employers.

rate.headline: 9% of payroll: SENA 2%, ICBF 3%, family compensation funds 4%
details: Employers with total payroll under 10 minimum wages per worker are exempt from SENA and ICBF.

instruments.explanation: Earmarked contributions for training, child welfare and family subsidies.
exceptions: Non-profit and some other entities are exempt.

names.official: Regalías por explotación de recursos naturales no renovables (Sistema General de Regalías)

taxes.base: Value of oil, gas, coal, minerals and other non-renewable resources extracted.

rate.headline: Percentage of production value by resource
details: Royalty rates by resource are set by law (for example a scale for hydrocarbons); the proceeds are distributed to territories through the SGR.

instruments.explanation: The State owns subsoil resources, so companies pay royalties, not taxes. The system shares them among producing and non-producing territories.
exceptions: The SGR is a biennial budget separate from the national budget.

names.official: Impuesto sobre vehículos automotores

taxes.base: Commercial value of vehicles registered in the department.

rate.headline: 1.5%, 2.5% or 3.5% by vehicle value band
details: Departments choose within these legal bands; 20% of revenue is shared with the municipality where the vehicle is registered.

instruments.explanation: An annual tax collected by the department.
exceptions: Motorcycles under 125 cc are excluded.

names.official: Impuesto de registro

taxes.base: Registration of deeds, company documents and other acts before notary and chambers of commerce.

rate.headline: 0.5% to 1% of the value of registered acts
details: Departmental assemblies set the rate within national limits.

instruments.explanation: A tax on registering property and corporate acts.
exceptions: Some public-interest acts are exempt.

names.official: Impuestos al consumo de cerveza, licores, vinos, aperitivos y cigarrillos
names.native: Impuesto al consumo de cerveza, licores y cigarrillos
names.common: Beer, liquor and tobacco consumption taxes

taxes.base: Beer, spirits, wine and cigarettes sold in the department.
taxes.payer: Producers and importers; passed on in prices.

rate.headline: Set by national law; ad valorem and specific components
details: Departments collect these taxes but the rates are fixed by national law.

instruments.explanation: Departmental excise taxes on alcohol and tobacco, an important source of health and education funding.
exceptions: Liquor tax rules changed by Ley 1816 de 2016.

names.official: Estampillas departamentales (pro-cultura, pro-universidad, pro-hospital, etc.)

taxes.base: Contracts and administrative acts with the department and its entities.

rate.headline: Varies by department and stamp
details: Each stamp is authorised by a national law and adopted by departmental ordinance with a percentage rate within a legal cap.

instruments.explanation: Small earmarked charges on public contracts for culture, universities, hospitals and the elderly.
exceptions: Caps and shares differ by stamp.

names.official: Impuesto predial unificado

taxes.base: Cadastral value of urban and rural property.

rate.headline: 5 to 16 per thousand of cadastral value (0.5%–1.6%)
details: Municipal councils set the rate within the legal band; lower for low-value housing.

instruments.explanation: The main municipal property tax; in Bogotá it is the second-largest tax after the ICA.
exceptions: Municipalities update cadastral values on national timetables.

legalRefs.locator: art. 4, rate band as modified by Ley 1450 de 2011 art. 23

names.official: Impuesto de industria y comercio (ICA) y complementarios

taxes.base: Gross receipts from industrial, commercial and service activities in the municipality.

rate.headline: 2 to 10 per thousand of gross receipts by activity
details: Municipal councils set rates within national ranges (industry 2–7‰, commerce and services 2–10‰).

instruments.explanation: A tax on business turnover; in cities like Bogotá and Medellín it now raises more than the property tax.
exceptions: Businesses in the SIMPLE regime pay ICA inside the single payment.

names.official: Sobretasa municipal a la gasolina motor

taxes.base: Gasoline sold at retail in the municipality.

rate.headline: Set by each municipal council within a legal cap
details: The cap is a percentage of the reference sale price.

instruments.explanation: A surcharge earmarked for road and transport investment.
exceptions: Departments levy a corresponding surcharge on diesel (ACPM).

names.official: Impuesto de alumbrado público

taxes.base: Users of public lighting service, usually billed with electricity.

rate.headline: Varies by municipality
details: Municipal councils set rates by user category under national rules.

instruments.explanation: A local charge to fund public lighting; its legal design has been litigated repeatedly.
exceptions: Bogotá adopted a property-tax surcharge to finance new lighting in 2024.

names.official: Participación en plusvalía y contribución de valorización

taxes.base: Increases in land value from planning decisions (plusvalía) or public works (valorización).

rate.headline: Plusvalía: 30%–50% of the value gain; valorización: cost recovery
details: Municipal councils decide the participation between 30% and 50% of the gain.

instruments.explanation: Special contributions that recover part of the public-created land value; classified as contributions, not taxes.
exceptions: Not applied in every municipality.
